title: God Tells the Truth About the Road

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Then the Lord said to him, "Know for certain that for four hundred years your descendants will be strangers in a country not their own and that they will be enslaved and mistreated there. But I will punish the nation they serve as slaves, and afterward they will come out with great possessions." - Gen 15:13-14 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God has just promised Abram a land and countless descendants. Now He tells him the rest: four hundred years of being strangers, of slavery and mistreatment, before the promise arrives. God does not hide the hard road. He tells Abram the truth.

This is worth noticing carefully. God did not promise a smooth journey. He promised a certain destination. Between the promise and its fulfilment lay centuries of suffering - and God says so plainly, in advance.

We often assume that if God has promised something good, the road there will be easy. Genesis 15 says otherwise. God's promises are certain, but the path to them frequently runs through hardship. Anyone selling you a version of faith without suffering is not selling you the Bible.

But look at the two anchors God gives. First: "I will punish the nation." God sees injustice and will deal with it. Second: "afterward they will come out." The suffering has a time limit and an ending. Paul knew this: "our light and momentary troubles are achieving for us an eternal glory that far outweighs them all" (2 Cor 4:17). God tells you the truth about the road - and He guarantees the destination.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Do you expect God's promises to come without hardship?
- What "afterward" can you hold onto in your current difficulty?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, thank You that You tell me the truth about the road, and that You guarantee the destination. When the journey is hard, help me hold onto Your "afterward" and trust Your faithfulness.
Amen.
